blocks.quote: Mixture of Three Energy Supply Systems Each cyclist’s power curve is unique,
due to different features of their energy supply system.
because of the better performance of ATP-CP energy supply system,
which is the main energy supply system for short and extremely intense exercise.
ATP is the direct energy source of the human body.
The ATP production speed and output power interrelated through a constant — the energy contained in unit ATP µ.
only a small amount of ATP is stored in the cells,
and can exist for only 1-3s during intense exercise.
The subsequent energy supply mainly relies on ATP regeneration.
There are three energy supply system in human body that can produce ATP to provide energy.
The overall output power is regarded as the sum of output power of each energy supply system:
are now going to discuss the ATP production of each energy supply system.
ATP-CP System The decomposition of intracellular creatine phosphate (CP) can provide energy and inorganic phos- phate,
VCP (t = 0) = MCP where VCP is the CP concentration in human body,
MCP is the maximum storage of CP in human body,
the number of ATP produced by decomposing unit CP,
vCP is the decomposition rate of CP.
Due to the limitation of the actual biological structure,
the speed of ATP production must be physi- ologically limited.
The ATP-CP process can be carried out under both anaerobic and aerobic conditions,
and the dura- tion is about 6–8 seconds.
the major energy supply system for short-time and intense exercise.
Restoration of CP During aerobic breathing,
the CP concentration in the human body is restored.
the restora- tion time of CP is about 3 – 5 min.
Glycolysis-Aerobic System Glycolysis system and aerobic system cooperate closely with each other.
therefore consider them together in this subsection.
Schematic diagram of glycolysis and aerobic energy supply system Under anaerobic conditions,
glucose is degraded by glycolysis to produce lactate and ATP,
and most of the energy is stored in lactate.
This process is also a preparation pathway for glucose oxidative metabolism.
lactate continues to decompose through oxidative metabolism to generate a large amount of ATP for energy.

VO2 is oxygen concentration of human body,
vin is the speed of lung providing oxygen for human body,

Restoration of Glycolysis Subsystem When the lactate concentration reaches the lactate threshold MLA ,
Glycolysis can con- tinue only if the glycolysis system is restored by decomposing lactate through aerobic respiration.
And when oxygen concentration in human body is insufficient,
the intensity of aerobic respiration will also be inhibited.
